key_insight: V-PaSS improves predictions for perovskite solar cells with unfamiliar materials by representing alloy physics and device-stack chemistry rather than treating materials as arbitrary labels.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support screening of new absorber alloys and transport-layer combinations beyond previously recorded device designs.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, cell polarity and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: On institution-grouped tests using unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with reported error reductions of 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Accuracy for compositions outside the 23-endpoint representation or alloys that depart from its interpolation assumptions remains uncertain.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
